title: test-0035-GEN-DISASTERS
passage: Dear Diary, today our school held a disaster preparedness workshop. My teacher explained that during an earthquake, we must immediately 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' under a sturdy table to protect ourselves from falling debris, rather than standing in doorways or near windows which are dangerous. She emphasized that even if the shaking stops, we must stay put because aftershocks are common and just as deadly. I learned that we should never use candles or matches to check for damage, as a gas leak could cause an explosion. We also discussed floods and cyclones. I was shocked to learn that floodwater is never clean, even if it looks like rainwater, because it carries sewage and chemicals. My teacher warned that we should never walk through it. Regarding cyclones, she explained that the calm eye is not the end of the storm; the winds will return with even greater force from the opposite direction. Therefore, if authorities issue an evacuation order, we must move to a cyclone shelter immediately, regardless of how strong our house feels. We must never wait until the winds start to leave, as by then, it will be too late to travel safely. Preparedness is our best defense.
